operations.text: 0.2.7 gives an installation one operator-owned page and gives a release note a way to say what it retires. THE TRANSFER SURFACE: a fresh install now seeds a skeleton at the configured `paths.transferSurface`, or at `<plansDir>/PNP_CANDIDATES.md` when that optional key is absent - four sections (Candidates, Ruling ledger, Pass statistics, Event ledger) for the work that is only proposed, the rulings that settled a conflict, what each auditor pass cost, and the rule-class events worth a pointer. It is seeded ONCE and then it is yours: no bookkeeping entry, no resolvable address, and no migration operation may ever address it, which is why this migration does not create it on your project. If you are updating rather than installing fresh, create it by hand - the skeleton is written out verbatim in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` under the transfer-surface heading, and setting `paths.transferSurface` in your `aiwf.config.json` is optional (without it the doctrine and the skills read the default path above). Nothing reads the key in the update engine or in the hooks, so adding it changes no behaviour you already have. SUPERSEDED IDS: a `note` operation may now carry an optional `supersedes` list, and the CHANGES report prints each entry as a `Supersedes: <id>` line under the note that retires it. It applies nothing - a note never writes a file of yours - so the ids are a list to read and act on, in whatever your own installation calls those records. This release retires five: `orchestrator-regulation-v2-seed`, `local-multisession-invariant`, `local-resume-economics`, `local-chain-trace-duty` and `local-stats-methodology`. THE ONE ARTIFACT OF YOURS THIS TOUCHES: the `aiwf-core` region of your CLAUDE.md, which this migration re-renders, because two sentences inside those markers changed with this release. The newborn-ticket paragraph now carries ONE question - does this ticket get an audit pass - and the answer lands in the ticket's PLAN entry; a question, never an automatic pass, so a pass you would pay for is asked for rather than announced to you. And the countable-tripwire list gains a fourth entry: an enumeration ends on a closing grep - for the symbol, for the phrase or count the change invalidates, and for the bare pointer form - that first HITS the known list and then returns zero outside it, and every new or changed evidentiary instrument is made to fail on purpose before it is trusted. Your own text OUTSIDE the region markers is untouched: the operation replaces what stands between the markers and nothing else. An artifact you hold through an override is not applied at all - the new render is recorded as upstream and the CHANGES report says so. And the distinction this note now has to make plainly, because it announces both kinds of thing at once: that operation addresses `CLAUDE.md#aiwf-core` and nothing else. The transfer surface is not the artifact being re-rendered and never becomes one - no bookkeeping entry, no resolvable address, no migration operation, not in this release and not in a later one. If this release introduces a word-gate: check your local rules for self-initiated dispatch or remediation - a rule written before this gate may contradict it.
